issues.description: Method name mismatch: The problem statement (UML) declares a public method Stock.emptyStock(): void, but the template Stock class provides public void clearInventory() instead. The solution repository implements public void emptyStock(). This naming inconsistency (emptyStock vs clearInventory) will confuse students and can cause compilation or test failures when tests or the specification expect emptyStock() but the starter code only exposes clearInventory().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template match the problem specification and the solution by exposing public void emptyStock(). Either rename the existing template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a new public void emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). Ensure the method signature is exactly: public void emptyStock().

issues.description: Stock clearing method name mismatch: the problem statement (and the solution implementation) specify a method Stock.emptyStock(), but the template implementation declares a method named clearInventory(). All three refer to the same concept (clearing/emptying the stock inventory). This identifier difference forces students to map 'emptyStock' to a differently named method in the starter code and may lead to confusion or errors when students search for or implement the required method (and when automated tests expect emptyStock).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by renaming the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a public wrapper emptyStock() in the template that delegates to clearInventory() (e.g., public void emptyStock() { clearInventory(); }). This preserves behavior while removing the naming inconsistency.
